title: Sustainable GPU Thermal Budget & Tenant Prioritization Roadmap
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This roadmap describes a cross-team initiative to introduce energy- and thermal-aware GPU scheduling, tenant prioritization policies, and a thermal budget abstraction into Redwood's platform scheduler. The goal is to reduce peak thermal events, improve long-term GPU health, and allow predictable, cost-aware tenant behavior during regional thermal constraints without sacrificing customer SLAs for paid tiers.

Why this matters now:

- Increasing fleet density and higher sustained token throughput for some customers has led to more frequent thermal headroom events and emergency throttles (observed spike in GPU thermal_p95 events since Q2 2026).
- On-prem and Dedicated customers require predictable performance and clear behavior during thermal contention windows.
- Energy-aware scheduling provides operational savings (cooling, power capping) and supports sustainability reporting commitments.

Objectives (measurable):

1) Reduce emergency thermal throttles (GPU_THERMAL_EMERGENCY alerts) by 60% in target regions by Q4 2027.
2) Introduce a "thermal budget" concept per-tenant with soft/hard tiers, and publish deterministic tenant-facing behavior matrix by Q2 2027.
3) Maintain critical latency SLOs for Production (p95 < 400 ms for foreground short requests) for Gold/Enterprise customers during constrained windows 95% of the time.
4) Ship observability dashboards and an alerting taxonomy for thermal events and energy usage by Q3 2027.

Key concepts introduced:

- Thermal budget (TB): a rolling 24h quota representing acceptable sustained thermal output per tenant/pool. Tracked as TB_remaining_pct.
- Thermal headroom: per-GPU metric expressed as thermal_headroom_pct = (max_safe_temp - current_temp) / (max_safe_temp - idle_temp).
- Priority lanes: Gold, Standard, Best-effort. Precedence controls placement and preemption policies.
- Energy-aware bin packing: placement-service will prefer nodes with higher cooling headroom and lower recent sustained TDP.

High-level timeline and milestones:

- Q4 2026: Prototype scheduler hook and TB data model; run synthetic load experiments in staging.
- Q1 2027: Deploy thermal telemetry pipeline to metrics-store; create dashboard prototypes.
- Q2 2027: Implement tenant TB enforcement with soft throttles (token injection rate limiting) for Best-effort lane; public documentation for Dedicated customers.
- Q3 2027: Introduce region-level thermal-pressure routing (route to other regions or model-variant fallback) and automated alerts.
- Q4 2027: Hard enforcement, preemption for Best-effort during sustained thermal emergency windows; retrospective and KPI review.

Deliverables by milestone:

- Scheduler changes: new placement hints, TB bookkeeping APIs, and preemption hooks in scheduler-daemon.
- Runtime telemetry: gpu_thermal_headroom_pct, gpu_tdp_window_avg, tenant_tb_consumption_rate.
- Dashboards: "Thermal Budget Heatmap", "Regional Thermal Pressure", and "Tenant TB burn-down".
- Runbook updates: thermal-emergency-runbook and tenant-communication playbook.
- API: management API for tenants to view TB_remaining_pct and request temporary burst credits.

Concrete metrics and alert thresholds (initial recommendations):

- gpu_thermal_headroom_pct < 20% for 10m triggers WARNING (SRE paging optional).
- gpu_thermal_headroom_pct < 10% for 5m triggers CRITICAL (page oncall, begin emergency routing).
- regional_avg_tb_burn_rate > planned_rate_by_region + 30% for 15m triggers INVESTIGATE.
- tenant_tb_remaining_pct < 15% triggers tenant-notification (email + console banner) and auto-apply soft-throttle on Best-effort lane.

Observability and dashboards:

- Dashboard names and essential panels:
  - Thermal Budget Heatmap: per-region, per-cluster TB_remaining_pct and burn rate.
  - GPU Health Summary: fleet-level headroom percentiles, TDP window trends, GPU error rates.
  - Tenant Impact View: list tenants currently in soft-throttle, estimated restoration time.

- Suggested SLI set (token-level):
  - tb_burn_rate_latency_ms.p95 (time to apply throttle after threshold breach).
  - thermal_fallback_success_rate (percentage of reroutes that complete within 2s).

Example scheduler config snippet (YAML) to define tenant TB and policy:

# tenant-thermal-policy.yaml
tenant_id: "acme-corp"
priority_lane: "Best-effort"
thermal_budget:
  window_hours: 24
  budget_units: 100000   # abstract units mapped to sustained TDP*seconds
  soft_threshold_pct: 25
  hard_threshold_pct: 5
burst_credit:
  daily_topup: 5000
  purchasable: true

CLI examples (operator):

# Query tenant TB
redwoodctl thermal describe --tenant acme-corp --region us-west-2

# Allocate emergency burst credits (operator only)
redwoodctl thermal grant-burst --tenant acme-corp --amount 10000 --reason "customer QPS surge"

Rollout strategy and safety controls:

1) Canary: start with a single low-risk cluster in us-west-2; only Best-effort tenants are subject to soft throttles. Monitor TB burn-down and user-visible latency for 7 days.
2) Gradual expansion: promote to other clusters and allow Standard lane intervention if metrics stable.
3) Feature flags: implement via placement-service feature flag with runtime knob for enforcement (off | soft-only | hard).
4) Automatic rollback: if p95 latency for Gold customers increases > 10% sustained for 30 minutes, rollback enforcement and open incident.

Ownership and stakeholders:

- Product (ML infra PM): Marta Kuznetsova — roadmapping, pricing policy for burst credits.
- Scheduler & Placement: Evan Martinez — implementation of TB data model and preemption hooks.
- Serving Runtime: Li Wei — ensure runtime can accept preemption/resume semantics and KV-cache warmup strategies.
- SRE/Observability: Priya Nambiar — dashboards, alerts, and runbook updates.
- Customer Success: Daniel Ortiz — tenant communications and billing ops coordination.

Dependencies and blockers:

- Telemetry pipeline: must ingest per-GPU thermal and TDP metrics at 10s granularity (eng-infra delivery Q1 2027).
- Billing changes: support for burst-credit purchase and tracking (finance & billing team coordination).
- Hardware firmware constraints: some legacy racks lack fine-grained TDP telemetry; requires inventory mapping and fallbacks.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Overly-aggressive enforcement harms paid customer latency.
  - Mitigation: Strict rollout controls, enforced SLO guardrails, and feature-flagged enforcement limited to Best-effort initially.
- Risk: TB abstraction complexity confuses customers.
  - Mitigation: Simple default policies, visible console indicators, and explicit documentation with examples.
- Risk: False positives in thermal telemetry.
  - Mitigation: Use rolling windows and cross-check against GPU error counters before page escalation.

Runbooks and playbooks to update (high level):

- thermal-emergency-runbook: steps to identify affected clusters, trigger cross-region routing, and notify customers.
- tenant-communication-playbook: templated emails and console banners for different enforcement states.
- post-incident-retrospective-template: add TB-specific fields (burn-rate, corrective action, credit allocs).

Acceptance criteria (for GA):

- Telemetry: full data ingestion and dashboard coverage for top 3 regions.
- Functionality: TB accounting, soft-throttle enforcement, and operator burst-granting implemented.
- Reliability: no more than 2 rollbacks during canary expansion.
- Documentation: published customer-facing docs and internal runbooks.

Next immediate action items (first 30 days):

1) Scheduler & telemetry teams: agree on TB schema and metric names (owner: Evan Martinez) — action due 2026-11-01.
2) Observability: create initial dashboard templates in Grafana and a set of alerts (owner: Priya Nambiar) — action due 2026-11-15.
3) Product: finalize tenant-facing policy tiers and burst-credit pricing draft (owner: Marta Kuznetsova) — action due 2026-11-30.

Appendix: telemetry naming conventions (recommended)

- gpu_thermal_headroom_pct{region,cluster,gpu_id}
- gpu_tdp_window_avg{region,cluster,gpu_id,window=5m}
- tenant_tb_consumption_rate{tenant,region,window=1m}
- tenant_tb_remaining_pct{tenant,region}

Appendix: quick reproducible experiment

- Use the synthetic-load harness to generate 1.5x baseline sustained token throughput on a 4-node cluster and observe tb_burn_rate and headroom impact. Record baseline p95 latency, TB burn-rate, and GPU temps.

Contributors and acknowledgments:

Thanks to the scheduler, observability, and serving-runtime teams for early design reviews. Special thanks to the platform-costs working group for prioritizing energy-aware metrics in Q3 2026.
